findings.F1: After a day on which the coin fell and traded far more than usual, it rebounded. In the top quartile of 1-day volume against the 30-day average and the bottom tercile of the volatility-scaled 1-day return, the next day's excess return was +0.171 of a usual move (t 8.3, 3229 cases). The next 3 days' excess was +0.172 (t 5.2, 1051 cases), about +1.6 % against a usual 3-day move of 9.29 % and a trade cost of 0.22 %.
findings.F2: The rebound after a heavy-volume fall grows with the volume. Across 1-day volume quartiles 0 to 3, the next-day excess after a falling day was −0.042, −0.008, +0.012 and +0.171. In a regression of the 3-day excess on log volume ratio, bar return and their interaction on down bars, the interaction has coefficient 0.052 (t 4.6, about 11 900 cases).
findings.F3: The heavy-volume-fall rebound holds on most coins and years, but not in the two bear years. Its 3-day excess is positive on 18 of 19 coins (INJ −0.146, the exception) and in 6 of 8 years, with t above 2.3 in 2019, 2020, 2021, 2024 and 2025. It is negative in 2018 (−0.104) and 2022 (−0.063).
findings.F4: A rise on thin volume gave part of itself back over the next three days. In the bottom quartile of 1-day volume and the top tercile of 1-day return, the 3-day excess was −0.160 of a usual move (t −5.0, 652 cases). Across volume quartiles 0 to 3 it rose steadily: −0.160, −0.047, +0.010, +0.061.
findings.F5: The tested volume-surge effect comes mostly from surges on falling bars. In the top quintile of the 4h volume ratio, the 3-day excess was +0.143 (t 4.2, 1165 cases) after a down bar and +0.069 (t 1.9, 1207 cases) after an up bar. In the bottom quintile it was negative on both sides: −0.094 (t −3.6) and −0.072 (t −2.8).
findings.F6: The book is mostly the coin held long, not the signal. It holds a position on 88 % of bars, with a mean allocation of 0.74. It takes about 64 % to 67 % of the coin's daily moves both ways: −4.06 % on the coin's worst-quintile days (coin −6.38 %) and +4.79 % on its best (coin +7.14 %).

ideas.idea: After a day on which a coin falls while trading far more than its 30-day average volume, it rises over the next one to three days. The heavier that day's volume against its average and the deeper the 1-day fall, the larger the rebound.
ideas.consequence: A heavy-volume sell-off is a reason to lean long for the next one to three days rather than follow the fall.
ideas.name: heavy-volume fall rebound

ideas.idea: After a day on which a coin rises on volume below its 30-day average, it gives back part of the rise over the next three days. The thinner the volume against its average and the larger the 1-day rise, the larger the give-back.
ideas.consequence: A rise on thin volume is a reason to refuse a long, or to lean short, over the next three days.
ideas.name: thin-volume rise give-back
